findings.title: Privileged trigger checks out untrusted code before Codex

evidence.description: Privileged workflow checks out attacker-influenced code before Codex runs.
evidence.snippet: - name: Checkout PR head in privileged workflow

findings.why_it_matters: Detects pull_request_target or workflow_run workflows that check out PR head or workflow-run code before Codex or write-capable steps.
findings.safer_pattern: Do not checkout untrusted head code in privileged jobs. Use pull_request with read-only permissions or split into an unprivileged job.
findings.false_positive_notes: Checking out the base branch on pull_request_target is not the same as checking out attacker-controlled head code.

findings.title: Codex uses danger-full-access or unsafe strategy without trusted trigger or gate

evidence.description: Codex is configured with danger-full-access.
evidence.snippet: - name: Run Codex with full access

findings.why_it_matters: Detects dangerous sandbox or safety strategy choices, especially on untrusted triggers.
findings.safer_pattern: Prefer read-only or workspace-write with privilege reduction. Add actor allowlists, maintainer labels, environments, or manual dispatch.
findings.false_positive_notes: Some self-hosted or Windows workflows may require unsafe strategy. They still need trusted prompts and tight gating.

findings.title: Untrusted content reaches Codex prompt in write-capable job

evidence.description: The untrusted prompt source shares a job with secrets, write permissions, OIDC, or write-capable sinks.

findings.why_it_matters: Escalates CODX001 when the same job has write permissions, secrets, OIDC, deployment access, or later write-capable side effects.
findings.safer_pattern: Split read-only Codex generation from write-capable follow-up jobs and require schema validation plus a trusted gate before any write.
findings.false_positive_notes: The rule is confidence-sensitive. If the job only has read permissions and no write sink, CODX001 should be the primary finding.

findings.title: OpenAI or Codex API key exposed at job scope with repo-controlled code

evidence.description: API key is exposed at job scope while the job checks out or runs repository-controlled code.

findings.why_it_matters: Flags job-level OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY when the job checks out or runs repository-controlled code.
findings.safer_pattern: Pass secrets only to the Codex action input or the smallest possible step scope. Avoid job-level env for model API keys.
findings.false_positive_notes: Step-scoped use directly on openai/codex-action is the expected safe shape and should not trigger this rule.

findings.title: Codex output feeds sensitive sink without schema validation
findings.downstream_sink: Execute Codex output: shell command consumes Codex output

evidence.description: Codex output feeds a sensitive downstream sink without output-schema validation.

findings.why_it_matters: Detects Codex final messages or output files consumed by shell, github-script, gh, release, deploy, package publish, merge, label, or comment automation without structured validation.
findings.safer_pattern: Require output-schema or output-schema-file, validate with jq/ajv/jsonschema, and constrain downstream commands.
findings.false_positive_notes: Artifact upload alone is not treated as a sensitive sink. The rule focuses on automation that changes external state.

findings.title: Untrusted GitHub event content reaches Codex prompt

evidence.description: Untrusted GitHub event content appears in a prompt file consumed by Codex.

findings.why_it_matters: Detects attacker-controlled GitHub event fields interpolated into Codex prompts, prompt files, stdin, or shell-generated prompt files.
findings.safer_pattern: Use static prompt files, pass only stable identifiers such as PR numbers, fetch untrusted text through a sanitizer, or require a maintainer-controlled gate.
findings.false_positive_notes: The finding may be acceptable when the source is strongly gated or only trusted maintainers can control the field. Keep the gate near the Codex invocation and document it.

profile_suggestions: Set explicit job-level permissions; read-only Codex jobs usually need contents: read and sometimes pull-requests: read.
Move static instructions into .github/codex/prompts and keep attacker-controlled text outside the prompt boundary unless gated.
Use output-schema-file before feeding Codex output to comments, releases, shell, gh, or deploy automation.
Add allow-users, actor checks, maintainer labels, protected environments, or workflow_dispatch-only entrypoints for write-capable workflows.
